In every icon the grey track is GENCODE; the coloured track is what flightcollapse emits. Faint dashed boxes are reference exons the model does not contain.

0.1.18 changes the 3′ end only — panel 5. Annotation may now refine a read-supported cleavage coordinate but never manufacture a distant one, and the polyA tail is read from each molecule instead of inferred from the genome.
Read admission
One definition of an admitted read, shared by the scanning
pass and the output pass, so the two can never disagree.
admitted
rejected
coverage ≥ 0.90 · identity ≥ 0.95 · 5′ soft clip ≤ 200 nt
On an untrimmed BAM the polyA tail is soft-clipped, so a 0.99 coverage
gate keeps only 6% of reads — and enriches for mono-exonic ones.
Junction census
Every junction in every admitted read is counted once, with
its motif, its flanking repeat, its share of the traffic at
each of its own splice sites, and its distance to the nearest
annotated site.
GENCODE
read
snapped
annotation-first: a read site within 5 bp moves onto the annotated site
internal deletions are promoted first
A short intron spelled as a CIGAR D rather than an N leaves
the intron chain untouched, so a real splicing event can hide
inside an "FSM". Gaps of 20–5,000 bp seen in ≥ 3 reads are
promoted to junctions before the census, then curated like
any other.
does the read have any intron?
YES → spliced track
NO → mono-exon track, panel 6
The empty chain is not a suffix of anything. That single rule is the
mono-exon fix.
Junction curation
Junctions are curated BEFORE chains are built. A chain with
40 reads containing one spurious junction survives a chain
threshold; it does not survive a junction threshold.
An ANNOTATED junction is never rejected — dropping one because it is
rare in one sample would fabricate novel chains out of well-known
transcripts.
a junction that is still novel must clear
molecules ≥ 3 and reads ≥ 5
not read count alone — reads are PCR copies
≥ 0.1% of the reads at its own donor AND its own
acceptor
was 1%. That threshold rejected 174 of 230 real junctions the
caller lost, and the ones it rejected carried 51 reads and 49.5
cells at the median against 13 and 12 for the novel junctions it
kept.
GT-AG always; GC-AG and AT-AC only with short-read
confirmation in ≥ 2 replicates, or ≥ 50 reads
was GT-AG only. That cost 8–10% of real junctions — including
SOD1's canonical transcript: GC-AG, 10,419 long reads, 1,005
short reads in 3 of 3 replicates.
no direct repeat ≥ 8 bp flanking the intron
RT template switching
local FDR ≤ 0.05 from the calibrated model
see below
the calibrated model the last bullet refers to
features
support · cells · reads-per-molecule · donor share · acceptor share ·
intron length · direct repeat · motif class · distance to annotated sites
Ridge logistic → two-component mixture → local FDR, with Storey π₀
and a monotone fit, stratified by whether the junction reuses an
annotated splice site. Annotated junctions are the positive
anchor; junctions on rejected reads are the negative one.
lfdr, posterior_real in junctions.tsv
why those two gates moved
Share and motif are already features of that model. It scored
the junctions the two hard gates were rejecting at lFDR 0.000
— confidently real — and the thresholds overruled it on its
own inputs. That is what 0.1.16 removes: not a loosening, a
de-duplication.
a read carrying a rejected junction is set aside
read
rejected junction
It never becomes a model — and it becomes the negative anchor the
chain-level model trains on. Relaxing the gates shrinks that set
as a side effect, and an empty decoy set makes the chain
calibration fall back to flat thresholds silently, so 0.1.16
counts decoy groups and fails the run below a floor.
decoy_chain_groups in qc.json
short reads are an anchor, never a filter
Short reads may SAVE a junction and can never condemn one. At
24% unique mapping, "the short reads did not see it" is not
evidence of absence — 227 of 525 known-real junctions were
invisible in all three replicates.
rescue is opt-in: junctions.short_read_rescue
Chain identity
Reads are grouped on the exact curated intron chain, stored
in transcript orientation so that a 5′-truncated read is
always a SUFFIX of its parent.

The representative is ALWAYS the maximal chain: merges only
ever run from a shorter chain into a longer one.
Terminal ends
3′ is the anchored end under oligo-dT, so it is
peak-clustered. 5′ is the degraded end: a model's 5′ end is
the 90th percentile of its members, never the minimum.
Ends are compared against EVERY transcript sharing the chain, not
against one designated parent.
new in 0.1.18 · a PCR family no longer picks the site
Peaks are found, ranked and placed on MOLECULE mass — each
read weighted 1/(reads sharing its cell+UMI). Support gates
still count whole reads and whole molecules; only the
geometry changed. On an already deduplicated BAM every weight
is 1 and this is a no-op.
weight_ends_by_molecule
new in 0.1.18 · polyA evidence comes from the molecule
The 3′ soft clip is read as SEQUENCE, not just measured. A
template-free A-run outside the alignment (poly-T on a
minus-strand read) is the only per-molecule evidence that
this coordinate is a cleavage site. Median 96% of a model's
molecules carry one; models flagged for internal priming
carry a 12 bp tail against 28 bp elsewhere.

An annotated alternative end, not a discovery. Checking only the
parent transcript undercounts badly: 35% of 3′ ends match it, 72%
match some transcript of the gene.

GENCODE

AAAA…tail
A genuine alternative polyA site. In 0.1.16 the evidence was
genomic — a PAS hexamer and downstream A-content, both statements
about the LOCUS. The tail is a statement about the molecule that
was primed there, and it is what decides now.

peak rejected, but an annotated end is within 300 bp

Snapped. This is annotation REFINING an observed coordinate, and
it stays: the median model still moves 6 bp and no model moves
more than 300.

peak rejected and the nearest annotated end is far away
read 3′ ends
moved 11.9 kb
0.1.16 re-labelled the peak with the parent's annotated end at ANY
distance — at NSL1 that put the model 11.9 kb past every read
supporting it, and it happened to 19,145 peaks per sample at a
median of 1.2 kb. The observed coordinate now stands and the model
says it is unresolved.
ENST…|end3_unresolved_1
A-rich genomic window downstream, no tail on the reads
model
A-rich, no tail
Still discarded as internal priming. The oligo-dT primes on
genomic A's, which ALIGN rather than clip — so an internally
primed molecule shows a read pile and no tail. That is the one
thing the read pile alone cannot tell you.
5′ end upstream of the annotated TSS
GENCODE
model
A credible alternative start — unless it crosses an annotated
junction, which makes it a retained first intron instead. A 5′
truncation, by contrast, is degradation and is absorbed into the
parent.
ENST…|ext5end1
parent_transcript — identical chain, nothing weaker
A PARENT is only ever a GENCODE transcript whose intron chain
equals the model's, within the ±5 bp fuzzy tolerance. Every
terminal-end category has one by construction. NIC and NNC
have a novel chain, so they have NO parent —
parent_transcript is empty for 100% of NIC and NNC models.
From chains.py: ref.transcripts_for_chain(). Among those, the one whose
annotated 3′ end is nearest the dominant peak.
associated_transcript — merely the closest
Separately, EVERY model is matched to its nearest reference
transcript — scored on shared, model-only and reference-only
junctions, then |3′ distance|, then |5′ distance| — as
associated_transcript. Where both exist they agree 98.7% of
the time, which is why conflating them looks harmless until a
NIC or NNC shows up.
Annotation only. It never feeds back into calibration, and it never
changes which model is emitted. A model NAME falls back to it when there
is no parent, so ENST…|NNC_1 names a neighbour, not a parent.
Mono-exon track
Runs entirely separately. Unspliced reads only ever group
with each other, so a single-exon stub can never absorb
spliced read mass.
inside the last exon or 3′UTR of a known gene
GENCODE
model
Trusted: with polyA capture this is RT drop-off in a long 3′UTR,
and the 3′ end is still correct.

Internal priming — discarded in every case. Note the 0–100 scale:
comparing this to 0.6 flags essentially everything.
Invariants — checked every run
mono-exon read mass ≈ unspliced read fraction
9.2% of reads unspliced against 57.9% of read mass on single-exon
models is how the isoseq bug was found.
model_is_min must not be ≈ 1.0
If the model is always the shortest member of its own group, the
representative rule is inverted.
median log2(read span / model span) ≈ 0
Reads should match the footprint of the model they were assigned to.
unspliced reads are accounted for
Reads that vanish are as much a modelling failure as reads that pile
onto a stub — just a quieter one.
the decoy set has not collapsed
Below 2,000 decoy chain groups the chain-level model has no negative
anchor and reverts to flat thresholds — silently, until 0.1.16 made
it fail.
rejected junctions carry LESS evidence than kept ones
qc.md prints rejections per rule with the median reads and lFDR of
each. A rule discarding junctions at lFDR 0.000 is visible on any run
instead of taking a masking experiment to find.
no 3′ end has moved further than the bound
New in 0.1.18. qc.md reports max_abs_tts_shift; it is 300 by
construction, so a larger value means a second code path is moving
ends and is a bug.
the polyA tail was actually measured
New in 0.1.18. A hard-clipped or trimmed BAM yields zero tails, which
is indistinguishable from 'no molecule had one' — so the report says
which.
unspliced reads skip panels 3-5 entirely
Outputs
sorted GTF / GFF · read_stat.txt (read-name keyed) · group.txt · abundance.txt · models.tsv · junctions.tsv (with drop_reason) · group_chains.tsv · cell × transcript UMI matrix · qc.json / qc.md
Support is counted in MOLECULES — UMI-collapsed per cell — not in reads. Thirty reads from one molecule is a PCR artefact, not evidence.
